sights.name: Chiringashima Island

sights.description: Japan's oldest herb garden with over 10,000 fragrant camphor trees; oils, herb tea, Sunday library.

sights.name: Hirakiki Shrine
sights.description: Called Satsuma's Ichinomiya for safe navigation and fishing; main hall is a prefectural cultural property.

sights.name: Tamanoi Well
sights.description: Japan's oldest well, used by Empress Toyotamahime; ruins remain, with early-spring rape blossoms nearby.

sights.name: Kaimon Foothills Nature Park
sights.description: Japan's largest subtropical botanical garden, with about 100,000 plants and touchable Tokara horses.

sights.name: Ibusuki Shrine

sights.name: Fudozan Seiryu-ji
sights.description: Shingon temple opened in 1990 at 300 meters, with a complex rare in Kyushu and a monk-made garden.

sights.name: Ibusuki Rapeseed Flower Fields

sights.name: Yamagawa Salt Factory Ruins

activities.name: Saido Beach
activities.description: North Sakurajima beach about ten minutes by car from the ferry port, beside a free black-pine park.

activities.name: Sakurajima Ferry
activities.description: A 15-minute sea bypass ferry between Kagoshima City and Sakurajima, linking the Satsuma and Osumi peninsulas.

activities.name: Roadside Station Kiire (Marinepia Kiire) Hachiman Onsen
activities.description: Alkaline simple onsen on Route 226 at Marinepia Kiire, with baths overlooking Sakurajima and Kinko Bay.

activities.name: Yaeyama Park and Camp Village
activities.description: Park above Iriki Pass with Sakurajima views, play areas, grass skiing, hiking, cottages and camping.

activities.name: Hozan Hall (Kagoshima Prefectural Culture Center)
activities.description: Opened in 1966 for plays, concerts, and meetings; its fourth floor has a planetarium and dinosaur fossils.

activities.name: Rainbow Beach
activities.description: Calm golden beach on Sakurajima beside Sakurajima Port, 100 meters long, with showers, family swimming, and kayaking.

activities.name: Sakurajima Lava Nagisa Park Footbath
activities.description: About 100 m footbath, among Japan's largest, with reddish-brown spring water from 1,000 m underground.

activities.name: Jigen-ji Park
activities.description: Park around Jigen-ji ruins with clear streams, greenery, nature trails, and spring cherry blossoms.

activities.name: Kagoshima City Urban Agriculture Center
activities.description: About 30 ha center 12 km northwest of central Kagoshima at 180 m, with seasonal flower beds overlooking Sakurajima.

activities.name: Kagoshima Cultural Crafts Village
activities.description: Crafts village for pottery, wood, bamboo, and handicrafts, with Saigo Takamori's farm-hut site and observatory.

activities.name: Ferry Yakushima 2 Kagoshima Kinko Bay Summer Night Fireworks Viewing Cruise
activities.description: Watch 15,000 fireworks, Kyushu's largest class, leisurely from a moored ship that does not go offshore.

activities.name: Spa Land Rarakura
activities.description: Onsen, dining, and lodging with large baths, sauna, swimsuit spa zone, and training room.

activities.name: Meisen no Sato Koriyama Onsen
activities.description: Weakly alkaline simple spring from 627 meters underground, with open-air, bubble, and cascading baths.

activities.name: Yunoyama Natural Onsen
activities.description: Free-flowing weakly alkaline onsen near Saigo Nanshu's historic site, with family baths and moisturizing water.

activities.name: Ashikari Onsen
activities.description: Free-flowing super public bath in Kagoshima City with outdoor, cypress, jacuzzi, and sauna baths plus a restaurant.

activities.name: Nukumi Beach
activities.description: Shallow white-sand pine beach in Kiire, southern Kagoshima City. Nukumi Beach House offers free lockers and showers.

activities.name: Green Farm Kiire
activities.description: Harvest seasonal vegetables, make pizza and baumkuchen, cook, and study circular agriculture. Campsite, playground, trail, shop, and restaurant.

activities.name: Sakurajima Island View
activities.description: About 60-minute hop-on hop-off bus from Sakurajima Port visiting viewpoints and visitor centers.

activities.name: Sakurajima Natural Onsen Digging Experience (Arimura Coast)
activities.description: Dig slightly into Arimura Coast sand to find about 40 C hot spring and make a foot bath.

activities.name: Sakurajima Ferry Terminal (Kagoshima Main Port)
activities.description: Ferry between Kagoshima Port and Sakurajima Port in about 15 minutes, with striking Sakurajima views and sometimes dolphins.

activities.name: Dolphin Waterway (Io World Kagoshima Aquarium)
activities.description: Watch dolphin training in a waterway connected to Kinko Bay.

activities.name: Sakurajima Lava Nagisa Park
activities.description: Roughly 100-meter foot bath of reddish-brown natural hot-spring water from 1,000 meters under Sakurajima.

activities.name: Kuromatsu Waterfront Park
activities.description: Sea-breeze-resistant black-pine windbreak contrasting with Sakurajima, chosen among 77 views, beside Nishimichi Beach.

activities.name: Nangoku Country Club
activities.description: A strategic course with excellent access and panoramic views of Kinko Bay and Sakurajima.

activities.name: Kagoshima Garden Golf Club
activities.description: A fine location overlooking Sakurajima to the east, for fulfilling golf amid nature-rich land.

activities.name: Daikoku Onsen
activities.description: Showa-era simple onsen with refreshing Kotsuki River wind, popular moisturizing beauty bath. Indoor and day-visit baths.

activities.name: Shiroyama Choju-sen
activities.description: Chloride spring facing the Shiroyama Observatory bus stop, with rock bath, sauna, cascade bath and cold bath.

activities.name: Hanano Onsen Tanuki-yu
activities.description: Emerald-green free-flowing hot spring from two sources, with a local-stone cave sauna. Simple spring; day-use bathing.

activities.name: Shin Toso Onsen
activities.description: Soak while viewing Kagoshima city and Sakurajima. Chloride spring with indoor bath, sauna, hot-spring pool, and day-use bathing.

activities.name: Satsuma Izaku Washi
activities.description: Edo-period Kagoshima washi making. Make postcards and mini lamps using memories or Sakurajima ash in 60-90 minutes.

activities.name: Kanmachia
activities.description: Paid outdoor and covered event plazas and meeting rooms, plus a local park with Sakurajima views.

activities.name: Sakurajima Daikon Harvest at Farmland Sakurajima
activities.description: Harvest giant Sakurajima daikon grown without pesticides or chemical fertilizers; it is Guinness-recognized.

activities.name: Kamoike-Tarumizu Ferry
activities.description: Ferry with 25 daily round trips between Kamoike and Tarumizu, about 40 minutes, passing Sakurajima.

activities.name: Marine Pier Kiire
activities.description: Onsen baths, sauna, year-round indoor pool, multipurpose plaza, and roadside station with specialties and restaurant.

activities.name: Kagoshima Bay Cruise
activities.description: Small-group cruise on calm Kinko Bay for Sakurajima views unseen from land, approaching Kanze and Okogashima.

activities.name: Secret Base N Farm
activities.description: A secret play area in fields, bamboo, and woods offering seasonal cooking, craft, and farm experiences.

activities.name: Waterfront Park
activities.description: Park near Kagoshima Port with Sakurajima and Kinko Bay views, a fountain, event plaza, and year-round events.

activities.name: Ikumi Beach
activities.description: Shallow beach of white sand and pines, popular with families; a breakwater calms waves.

activities.name: Jigen-ji Flowing Somen
activities.description: Summer flowing-somen tradition at Taniyama's Jigen-ji Park, with rice balls, grilled trout, and carp.

activities.name: Kagoshima City Kamoike Sea Fishing Park
activities.description: Sea fishing park on Kinko Bay with Sakurajima views; tackle and bait sold or rented for easy fishing.

activities.name: Kagoshima City Sakurajima Sea Fishing Park
activities.description: Easy fishing backed by Sakurajima; depth 6-9 meters, fairly fast current, capacity 45 anglers.

activities.name: Furusato Onsen
activities.description: Sakurajima onsen on the south shore facing Kinko Bay, with grand views and seaside open-air baths.

activities.name: Sakurajima Event Plaza Zone (Former Akamizu Quarry Site)
activities.description: About 30,000-square-meter event plaza overlooking Sakurajima, Kinko Bay, and Kagoshima City.

activities.name: Kagoshima Glamping Yoshizora
activities.description: Luxury camping in Yoshino Park on a hill overlooking Sakurajima, with dome and cabin lodges and BBQ.

activities.name: Kagoshima Fish Market Tour
activities.description: English-guided tour entering the fish market, normally closed to visitors, to experience auctions; breakfast not included.

activities.name: THE ROOF
activities.description: Tenmonkan rooftop bar and bistro using fresh Kagoshima ingredients, with Sakurajima views and cocktails.

activities.name: Kinko Bay Fishing Experience Hitomimaru
activities.description: Boat fishing facing Sakurajima on Kinko Bay, about five minutes from Tenmonkan; beginners and empty-handed visits welcome.

activities.name: Kinko Bay Fishing Experience (Boat Karin)
activities.description: Seasonal fishing around Kinko Bay and Sata Cape, from near-port waters to offshore and lure fishing.

activities.name: Sheraton Kagoshima
activities.description: Hotel with 228 rooms of 10 types, five restaurants and bars, and a free-flowing sodium chloride onsen.

sights.name: Arimura Lava Observatory
sights.description: 1946 lava-field observatory on a 1 km trail; close views of Sakurajima's active Minamidake crater and Kinko Bay.

sights.name: Former Kagoshima Spinning Mill Engineer's Residence
sights.description: Residence for British engineers invited for Japan's first Western-style spinning mill. Important Cultural Property and World Heritage.

sights.name: Meiji Restoration Hometown Museum
sights.description: History tourism facility on late-Edo Satsuma and the Meiji Restoration, in Saigo and Okubo's hometown Kajiya-cho.

sights.name: Okubo Toshimichi Bronze Statue
sights.description: Monument to Okubo Toshimichi, called one of the Meiji Restoration's three great figures, made by Shinya Nakamura in 1979.

sights.name: Kagoshima Prefectural History and Art Center Reimeikan
sights.description: Prefectural historical materials center built on Kagoshima Castle's main bailey site, rich in Restoration-era materials.

sights.name: Kagoshima City Museum of Art
sights.description: City art museum since 1954, with Kagoshima-born painters, Western art from Impressionism onward, Satsuma ware and cut glass.

sights.name: Io World Kagoshima Aquarium
sights.description: Aquarium facing Sakurajima with about 800 species, including Kyushu's only whale sharks in a large tank.

sights.name: Ishibashi Memorial Park and Museum
sights.description: Park with three restored late Edo arch stone bridges and a museum on bridge techniques and history.

sights.name: Saigo Takamori Statue
sights.description: Eight-meter bronze of Saigo Takamori in army general uniform, completed in 1937 at Shiroyama.

sights.name: Satsuma Gishi Monument
sights.description: Monument built in 1920 honoring 88 Satsuma samurai who died in the 1753 Horeki flood-control works.

sights.name: Xavier Park
sights.description: Park with remains of Xavier Church and statues of Francis Xavier, who landed in Kagoshima in 1549.

sights.name: Shoko Shuseikan
sights.description: Shimazu family history museum in Japan's oldest surviving Western-style factory, a World Heritage site since 2015.

sights.name: Shiroyama Park
sights.description: 107-meter hill with trails and an observatory viewing Sakurajima, Kinko Bay, and the city; Satsuma Rebellion sites.

sights.name: Sengan-en
sights.description: Shimazu family villa garden built in 1658, treating Sakurajima as a hill and Kinko Bay as a pond.

sights.name: Hayashi Fumiko Literary Monument and Furusato Park
sights.description: Furusato Park has two bronze statues and Hayashi Fumiko's literary monument; her mother was from Sakurajima.

sights.name: Kurokami Buried Torii
sights.description: The 1914 Sakurajima eruption buried Kurokami Shrine's torii, left unexcavated as a prefectural natural monument.

sights.name: Minato-odori Park
sights.description: Lawn-belt park from City Hall to the coastal road, with a lit stone monument, flat fountain, and year-end illumination.

sights.name: Xavier Landing Monument
sights.description: Stone monument in Gion-no-su Park facing Kinko Bay, commemorating Xavier's first Christian mission in Kagoshima in 1549.

sights.name: Kagoshima Prefectural Museum
sights.description: Natural history museum founded in 1953 introducing Kagoshima nature spanning 600 kilometers.

sights.name: Kagoshima City Science Museum
sights.description: Science museum on volcanoes and rockets, with a giant Sakurajima model and planetarium.

sights.name: Nagashima Art Museum
sights.description: Hilltop art museum among subtropical trees, overlooking Sakurajima, with about 1,000 works.

sights.name: Oasis Care Yoshino Park (Kagoshima Prefectural Yoshino Park)
sights.description: A 30-hectare lawn park in northeast Kagoshima with an observatory facing Sakurajima.

sights.name: Kodama Art Museum
sights.description: Kagoshima City's first private art museum, opened in 1985 on a wooded 85,600-square-meter site.

sights.name: Miyake Art Museum
sights.description: Displays Kagoshima-related paintings, Satsuma and Ryukyu ceramics, and contemporary Satsuma ware.

sights.name: Kagoshima Shimazu Family Cemetery (Fukusho-ji Ruins)
sights.description: Ancestral temple of the Shimazu family, preserved as their cemetery and abolished in 1869.

sights.name: Xavier Memorial Cathedral
sights.description: Completed in 1999 in Kagoshima to mark 450 years since Xavier's landing. Exterior evokes trading ships; seats 750.

sights.name: Terukuni Shrine
sights.description: Shrine to Shimazu Nariakira, 28th Shimazu head. Kagoshima City's largest, with a free museum and bronze statues.

sights.name: Karasujima Observatory
sights.description: Observatory overlooking Sakurajima and Kinko Bay on barren Taisho lava that buried the island of Karasujima.

sights.name: Sakurajima Visitor Center
sights.description: Exhibits on Sakurajima's eruptions, growth, plant succession, tourism, and disaster prevention, plus theater and dioramas.

sights.name: Yunohira Observatory
sights.description: Highest public viewpoint on Sakurajima at 373 meters, overlooking Minamidake, Kinko Bay, and Kagoshima.

sights.name: Sakurajima
sights.description: Kagoshima's symbol, a rare active volcano combining Kitadake and Minamidake, still emitting smoke and ash.

sights.name: Senganbira Nature Park
sights.description: At 577 meters, views of Sakurajima, Kaimondake, and a glimpse of Lake Ikeda; famous for azaleas.

sights.name: Shinya Nakamura Art Museum
sights.description: A rare sculpture museum in Japan beside sculptor Shinya Nakamura's studio, with about 1,000 works.

sights.name: Irisa Field God
sights.description: A 1727 field god statue backed by the huge Imoishi rock, a prefectural cultural property.

sights.name: Hanao Hidden Nenbutsu Cave
sights.description: Cave used for secret Jodo Shinshu practice while the Satsuma domain banned the sect.

sights.name: Hanao Shrine
sights.description: Shrine founded in 1218 by Shimazu Tadahisa and called Satsuma Nikko.

sights.name: Tango no Tsubone Tomb
sights.description: Dozens of stone pagodas at Hanao Shrine, including Tango no Tsubone's 1227 tomb.

sights.name: Statue of Lord Shimazu Tadayoshi
sights.description: 29th head of the Shimazu family, sculpted in 1917 by Fumio Asakura.

sights.name: Statue of Lord Shimazu Hisamitsu
sights.description: Bronze statue of Hisamitsu, Nariakira's brother and Tadayoshi's father, at Terukuni Shrine, made in 1917 by Fumio Asakura.

sights.name: Bronze Statue of Hirata Yukie
sights.description: Commissioner of the 1753 Kiso River flood control; 3-meter statue made in 1954 by Ando Shi.

sights.name: Bronze Statue of Admiral Togo Heihachiro
sights.description: Combined Fleet commander who defeated Russia's Baltic Fleet in 1905; 1.8-meter statue made in 1957 by Kohei Amada.

sights.name: Statue of Godai Tomoatsu
sights.description: Bronze statue of Godai, first head of Osaka's chamber of commerce, made in 1961 by Masakatsu Sakagami.

sights.name: Sakamoto Ryoma Honeymoon Trip Monument
sights.description: Bronze statue by Shinya Nakamura, installed in 1980, marks Ryoma and Oryo's 1866 Kirishima visit, called Japan's first honeymoon.

sights.name: Young Satsuma Statue Group
sights.description: Statues of Satsuma students sent to Britain in 1865, at Kagoshima-Chuo Station east exit plaza.

sights.name: Yozan Art Museum
sights.description: Currently closed. Opened in 1999; collection centers on Ebihara and Hirano, and it owns Van Gogh's Paris apartment.

sights.name: Jigen-ryu Heihojo Historical Museum
sights.description: Displays Jigen-ryu materials including Togo family documents; visitors can view the dojo, watch videos, or book experiences.

sights.name: Kagoshima Castle (Tsurumaru Castle) Goromon
sights.description: Imposing main gate of Tsurumaru Castle, burned in 1873 and restored in 2020 as Japan's largest castle gate.

sights.name: Shigakko Ruins
sights.description: Private school Saigo Takamori founded in 1873 for samurai; bullet marks remain in the walls. Prefectural historic site since 1968.

sights.name: Kagoshima Prefectural Office Observation Lobby
sights.description: About 93 meters up, the 18th-floor lobby views Kinko Bay, Sakurajima, and wide night scenery.

sights.name: Terayama Park
sights.description: Park at Yoshino Plateau's highest point with a Kinko Bay panorama observatory near World Heritage Terayama charcoal kiln ruins.

sights.name: Statue of Lord Shimazu Nariakira
sights.description: Bronze statue of 28th Shimazu head Nariakira, who began Shuseikan, promoting military, education, science, and industry. Fumio Asakura, 1917.

sights.name: Akamizu Observation Plaza
sights.description: Sakurajima looks wide and close from a lawn slope. The lava Portrait of the Scream marks Nagabuchi's 2004 all-night concert.

sights.name: Kagoshima Ken Gokoku Shrine
sights.description: Enshrines Kagoshima natives who died for the nation, and SDF, police, and firefighters killed on duty.

sights.name: Arata Hachimangu
sights.description: Branch shrine of Kagoshima Jingu built near the end of the Heian period, revered for safe childbirth and viper-warding sand.

sights.name: Former Shuseikan Reverberatory Furnace Ruins
sights.description: Reverberatory furnace at Shuseikan in Iso, based on Dutch texts to cast iron cannons; World Heritage component.

sights.name: Sakurajima Naval Base Ruins
sights.description: Late Pacific War Japanese Navy base; hand-dug tunnels about 650 meters held torpedo and power rooms.

sights.name: Site of Saigo Takamori's Death
sights.description: Site where Saigo Takamori, age 49, died on September 24, 1877, at the end of the Satsuma Rebellion.

sights.name: Birthplace of Saigo Takamori
sights.description: Saigo Takamori and brother Tsugumichi lived here until youth; Tsugumichi later was Navy and Home Minister.

sights.name: Site of Saigo's Take Residence
sights.description: Saigo Takamori lived here for four years from 1873 until the 1877 Satsuma Rebellion. His well remains.

sights.name: Packhorse Fall Monument
sights.description: Marks where Saigo's horse fell about 1.8 meters into a field while carrying seed sweet potatoes.

sights.name: Monument to Nanshu's Reclamation Site
sights.description: After returning in 1873, Saigo reclaimed about 39 hectares here with students, working the land himself.

sights.name: Site of Saigo's Country Residence
sights.description: Rural site where young Saigo farmed taro and sweet potatoes and often stayed alone.

sights.name: Grave of Monk Gessho
sights.description: Loyalist monk who died after throwing himself into Kinko Bay with Saigo in 1858.

sights.name: Saigo Family Graves
sights.description: Cemetery of Saigo Takamori's ancestors and family, with 23 old gravestones in three rows, relocated in 1922.

sights.name: Tsukiyomi Shrine
sights.description: Shrine said to have 1300 years of history, with pigeon and owl fortunes and a small observatory.

sights.name: Marine Port Kagoshima
sights.description: Domestic and international cruise ships dock here; lawn plaza and promenade suit walks, with a summer waterfront plaza.

sights.name: History Road: Meiji Restoration Drama Road
sights.description: Learn about Saigo Takamori and Okubo Toshimichi through a gate, seven monuments, and AR dramas.

sights.name: Historical Road Ishin Furusato no Michi
sights.description: Stroll past Saigo and Okubo sites, Ishin Furusato Hall, a song monument, history boards, and a reproduced samurai house.

sights.name: Former Shimazu Clan Tamazato Residence Garden
sights.description: Garden built in 1835 by the 27th Shimazu head Narioki, divided into upper and lower gardens.

sights.name: Site of Zoshikan, Embukan and Igakuin
sights.description: Zoshikan and Embukan were founded in 1773 by Shimazu Shigehide; Igakuin stood to the south.

sights.name: Tenpozan Battery Site (Anglo-Satsuma War)
sights.description: Eleven-cannon battery built in 1850 that opened fire first in the 1863 Anglo-Satsuma War.

sights.name: Former Residence Site of Saigo Nanshu (Kaminozono-cho)
sights.description: In 1855 Saigo's poor family moved here. Ryoma stayed one night and asked Ito for a loincloth.

sights.name: Place Where Okubo Toshimichi Grew Up
sights.description: Okubo moved here from Korai-cho as a child and grew up with Saigo, three years older.

sights.name: Birthplace of Okubo Toshimichi
sights.description: Birthplace of Okubo Toshimichi, active in the late Edo period and Meiji Restoration.

sights.name: Murata Shinpachi Birthplace Monument
sights.description: Monument at the 1836 birthplace of Murata Shinpachi, killed in the Satsuma Rebellion.

sights.name: Priest Gessho Historic Site Monument
sights.description: Monument at the Tawaraya inn site where detained monk Gessho later drowned in Kinko Bay with Saigo.

sights.name: Shinhatoba Battery Ruins
sights.description: Tuff stone battery built by Shimazu Nariakira; its shell struck British flagship Euryalus.

sights.name: Satsuma Rebellion Bullet Marks
sights.description: Former Shigakko stone walls have many hollows from government army bullets in the Satsuma Rebellion.

sights.name: Tagayama Park
sights.description: Admiral Togo statue faces Sakurajima across Kinko Bay, with aquarium facilities and Tofuku-ji Castle Ruins.

sights.name: Kawanabe Pass
sights.description: Highway curve overlooks Kagoshima, Sakurajima and Kinko Bay by day, and glittering ferries and cruise ships at night.

sights.name: Suzuyama Observatory (Ibusuki Skyline)
sights.description: Green below, indigo Kinko Bay, blue sky and Sakurajima harmonize, with birdsong and a gentle breeze.

sights.name: Susuhara Observatory (Ibusuki Skyline)
sights.description: Ridge from Sakurajima to the Takakuma Mountains across Kinko Bay is beautiful. A fine cherry tree stands beside it.

sights.name: Hidaka Observatory (Ibusuki Skyline)
sights.description: Views JX Kiire oil tanks, then Kinko Bay and Sakurajima. Orderly tanks blend with the bay and Osumi mountains.

sights.name: Nanshu Park
sights.description: Park holding Nanshu Shrine, a Seinan War cemetery, and Saigo memorial hall, with Sakurajima seen over the city.

sights.name: Haragosha Shrine
sights.description: Shrine built by Kurokami people who moved to Yoshino after the Anei eruption, enshrining deities invited from Kurokami.

sights.name: Yojirogahama Long Waterway
sights.description: A 1.6 km straight channel past the breakwater offers close Kinko Bay and Sakurajima views, colorful at sunrise and sunset.

sights.name: Taniyama Shrine
sights.description: Shrine to Prince Kaneyoshi overlooking Sakurajima, the Ibusuki-Makurazaki Line, and Taniyama city.

sights.name: Nanshu Bridge
sights.description: Pedestrian-only Kotsuki River bridge with cherry trees and Sakurajima visible past modern buildings.

sights.name: Sakurajima Local Products Hall Observatory
sights.description: Observatory views of slopes built by repeated eruptions and hardy pines; giant Sakurajima daikon sculpture photo spot.

sights.name: Satsuma Rebellion Army Headquarters Site
sights.description: Satsuma army headquarters during the Satsuma Rebellion; Don Plaza named for a cannon used as a noon signal.

sights.name: Kagoshima Environmental Future Museum
sights.description: Kagoshima City base for environmental learning and conservation, with hands-on exhibits on climate change and biodiversity.

sights.name: Iwaya Kannon
sights.description: Kannon and Fudo Myoo statues among huge rocks, about 15 minutes up through bamboo.

sights.name: Kagoshima Museum of Modern Literature and Kagoshima Fairy Tale Museum
sights.description: Introduces 28 Kagoshima-related writers; fairy-tale museum has trick art and a floating picture-book castle.

sights.name: Tenshoin Statue
sights.description: Statue of Tenshoin (Atsuhime), wife of the 13th shogun Tokugawa Iesada, who managed Edo Castle's inner palace.

sights.name: Furusato Archaeology and History Museum
sights.description: Hands-on museum on Kagoshima City history from the Paleolithic, using artifacts, videos, and experiential exhibits.

sights.name: Saigo Nanshu Memorial Museum (Nanshu Cemetery and Nanshu Shrine)
sights.description: Memorial museum on Saigo Takamori and Meiji Restoration pioneers, with Nanshu Shrine and cemetery.

sights.name: Shiokaze Street Boardwalk
sights.description: Planked walkway at the north wharf where you can sit and watch Sakurajima ferries in the sea breeze.

sights.name: Tenmonkan Site Monument

sights.name: Tsukazaki Kofun Group

sights.name: Uchinoura Kaizo Fortress Ruins
sights.description: Battery and observation post in Kaizo; seven cannons stood at six Shibushi Bay sites. Observation post entry is prohibited.

activities.name: Classic Grape Hamada Farm
activities.description: Grapes raised to classical music; grape and blueberry picking, mango sales, and fruit sauces.

day_to_day.name: Saigo Park
day_to_day.description: Free park in front of Kagoshima Airport with a 10.5-meter Saigo Takamori statue and tourist information.

day_to_day.name: Kirishima Onsen Market
day_to_day.description: Tourist information, souvenir shops and eateries, onsen-steamed eggs and vegetables, and a paid foot bath.

day_to_day.name: Black Vinegar Garden Pot Field Shop & Restaurant
day_to_day.description: Sakamoto Brewing has made pot-brewed black vinegar for 200 years; the shop and restaurant overlook pot fields and Sakurajima.

day_to_day.name: Kakushida Black Vinegar Village
day_to_day.description: Japan's first black-vinegar restaurant with pot-field tours and a shop, using home-grown JAS organic vegetables.

day_to_day.name: Kurobuta no Yakata Farm-Direct Restaurant
day_to_day.description: Serves Kagoshima black pork from partner cooperatives, including tonkatsu and shabu-shabu; local information base.

day_to_day.name: Koji Village Barrel Valley Praha & GEN
day_to_day.description: Learn, taste, and buy exclusive koji products and shochu. Czech village offers Pilsner and meals; GEN serves koji-raised black pork.

day_to_day.name: JR Kirishima-Jingu Station
day_to_day.description: Nearest station to national-treasure Kirishima Jingu, renewed March 2024 with Kagoshima cedar, food, crafts, and nearby cafe.

day_to_day.name: Kagoshima Airport Tourist Information Center
day_to_day.description: First-floor information desks in domestic and international arrival lobbies guide tourism, transport, hotels, and taxis.

day_to_day.name: Kagoshima Airport Multifunction Service Counter (Domestic Flights 1F)
day_to_day.description: Counter for domestic and overseas airport users, with English support and WiFi router rental.

day_to_day.name: Kimamana Kitchen
day_to_day.description: Hideaway shop in a Kirishima forest serving homegrown vegetable lunches and homemade sweets, with hammocks on site.

day_to_day.name: Yokogawa Kito
day_to_day.description: Cafe, select shop, and guesthouse in a renovated 1931 house, serving local handmade spice curry.

day_to_day.name: CAFE510
day_to_day.description: Warm, calm interior retaining former warehouse traces. Lunch ranges from quiche plates to set meals; pancake and cake sets recommended.

day_to_day.name: Kirishima Fumoto Station
day_to_day.description: Local products hall with fresh vegetables, bento, and Kagoshima specialties, plus a cafe serving gelato and drinks.

day_to_day.name: Toki Kirishima
day_to_day.description: Japanese tea cafe at the foot of the Kirishima mountains serving tea-based lunches, seasonal sweets, and Kirishima tea.

day_to_day.name: Obama Village
day_to_day.description: Future village in Kirishima's Obama district with seven shops, offices, a shared space, and barrier-free design.

day_to_day.name: mijicafe
day_to_day.description: Pet-friendly cafe opposite Kirishima Animal Hospital with lead hooks, terrace seats, and a small dog run.

day_to_day.name: Bakery and Cafe ReeNo
day_to_day.description: Stylish bakery cafe with over 70 kinds of bread, eat-in space, and three dog-friendly terrace tables.

activities.name: Kuroishidake Forest Park
activities.description: Recreation park in the forest of 524.7-meter Kuroishidake, with 360-degree views, bungalows, and tents.

activities.name: Kokubu Camp Beach
activities.description: Sandy beach about 700 meters long near Kokubu Interchange, with campsite, bungalows, showers, and a shop.

activities.name: Mizobe Uwadoko Park
activities.description: Sports grounds, tennis courts, children's water play, and views toward Sakurajima and Kirishima.

activities.name: Mizobe Fureai Onsen Center
activities.description: Barrier-free baths with jet, bubble, and low-frequency options, a sauna, and marble family baths.

activities.name: Yokogawa Health Onsen Center
activities.description: Men's and women's baths of 50 square meters each, with eight bath types and private family baths.

activities.name: Maruoka Park
activities.description: Meiji centennial park overlooking Kirishima, with Japan's longest go-kart track, rabbits, cherries, and azaleas.

activities.name: Kirishima Onsen (Maruo Area)
activities.description: Nine springs at 600-850 m southwest of Kirishima, a tourism base near falls and autumn foliage.

activities.name: Onami Pond
activities.description: Crater lake at 1,241 m on an easy 1,411 m peak; 1.9 km around and 11 m deep.

activities.name: Kirishima Plateau National Recreation Area
activities.description: Year-round cottages, auto campsite, onsen, tennis, cycling and ground golf, plus a summer pool and rentals.

activities.name: Kirishima Plateau Horse Riding Club
activities.description: One-on-one riding from beginner to experienced, a children's lead-horse course, and an all-weather indoor arena.

activities.name: Maruo Nature Trail
activities.description: About 2.3 km primeval-forest walk past Maruo Falls, Senjojiki, Nunobiki Falls and a rock bath called Kirishima's oldest.

activities.name: Hinode Onsen Kinoko no Sato
activities.description: Woody onsen by the Amori River with a cafe; spring diluted from 50 to about 42 degrees.

activities.name: Kirishima International Music Hall (Miyama Concert)
activities.description: About one-hour mini-concerts from classical to popular music for school trips and groups.

activities.name: Kagoshima Prefectural Kirishima Nature Interaction Center
activities.description: Forest animals emerge from the entrance clock to play music; camping capacity 150.

activities.name: Kirishima Mythology Village Park (Roadside Station Kirishima)
activities.description: Park at 670 meters overlooking Kinko Bay and Sakurajima, with rides, local goods, and blueberry picking.

activities.name: Kaminoyu Onsen Center
activities.description: Onsen center with family, bubble, and floating baths; two bathhouses swap genders daily.

activities.name: Takachiho Nature Trail
activities.description: Trail from Takachiho-gawara to the old shrine site, through forest with deer and a birdwatching hut.

activities.name: Kirishima Folk Craft Village
activities.description: Next to Kirishima Shrine, with a Yakusugi museum, Ryujin Kiln, restaurant, sweets, seasonal views, and a foot bath.

activities.name: Myoken Onsen
activities.description: Open-air baths amid deep greenery by the Amori River, known as a drinkable hot spring.

activities.name: Hinatayama Onsen Park
activities.description: A multipurpose park in 700-year-old Hinatayama Onsen, with about 120 cherry trees for spring viewing.

activities.name: Obama Beach
activities.description: Shallow, clean beach in Kirishima-Kinkowan National Park where you can swim while viewing Sakurajima.

activities.name: Kokubu Shiroyama Park
activities.description: 192 m hill park with Sakurajima views, a go-kart course, and a Ferris wheel.

activities.name: Kirishima Green Village
activities.description: National park sports facilities with grounds, tennis and volleyball courts, bungalows, communal onsen, kitchen, and meeting room.

activities.name: Kagoshima Airport Oyattosa Foot Bath
activities.description: Japan's first airport natural onsen foot bath; Oyattosa means well done in Kagoshima dialect.

activities.name: Ashibi no Yu Foot Bath at Kirishima-Jingu Station
activities.description: Simple hot spring at 40 to 45 degrees Celsius; admission is free.

activities.name: Kirishima Momiji Valley Seiryuso
activities.description: Quiet primeval-forest setting beside a stream, with abundant simple onsen, Japanese banquet food, indoor and open-air baths.

activities.name: Yoshida Onsen
activities.description: Known as a beauty bath that creates fair skin; a bicarbonate spring with indoor, private, and day-visit baths.

activities.name: Shusui-yu
activities.description: Soak in abundant bicarbonate spring water while hearing the Amori River; indoor and day baths.

activities.name: Myoken Ishihara-so
activities.description: Amori River inn with free-flowing bicarbonate spring; indoor, outdoor, private, and day-visit baths.

activities.name: Tenkei-so
activities.description: Hideaway inn with a free-flowing private bicarbonate spring, gorge beauty, and local organic breakfast.

activities.name: Kirishima Hideaway Inn Yuyu-an and Kirishima Beauty Onsen You-yu
activities.description: Weakly alkaline, colorless, odorless sodium bicarbonate spring famed for beautiful skin; Saigo Takamori praised it.

activities.name: Myoken Onsen Nemu
activities.description: Longtime cure spot 15 minutes by car from Kagoshima Airport, with abundant rock bath and Amori River gorge seasons.

activities.name: Sakura Sakura Onsen
activities.description: Natural mud bath rich in sulfur and other minerals. Apply, dry, and rinse for smooth skin.

activities.name: Suki no Yado Nokakutei
activities.description: Inn with 800 years of history in Hinatayama Onsen, loved by Saigo Takamori. Rock baths face gardens and stars.

activities.name: Kirishima Yunotani Mountain Lodge
activities.description: Wooden Japanese-style inn in virgin forest with a therapeutic-bath atmosphere. Sulfur spring.

activities.name: Hinatayama Onsen Center
activities.description: Bicarbonate spring with indoor baths and day-use bathing.

activities.name: Ten Terrace
activities.description: Views of Kirishima nature, starry skies, and distant Sakurajima. Private baths recommended for couples.

activities.name: Ryokojin Mountain Villa
activities.description: Quiet resort hotel on a 700-meter hill with private open-air baths and Sakurajima views.

activities.name: Kirishima Shinmoe Villa
activities.description: The only open-air bath, secluded at Kirishima's foot amid seasonal scenery at Shinyu Onsen.

activities.name: Wasure no Sato Gajoen
activities.description: Thatched roofs, hearth smoke, garden chickens, pesticide-free food, and a free-flowing bicarbonate spring.

activities.name: Kirishima-cho Distillery and Akarui Noson
activities.description: Shochu from Kirishima spring water in traditional clay pots. Tours, tastings, and label writing.

activities.name: Anraku Onsen Tsuru-no-Yu
activities.description: Semi-open-air bath facing the Amori River; waterfall and indoor baths. Bicarbonate spring; day use available.

activities.name: Tajima Honkan Toji Inn
activities.description: Historic therapeutic bath inn opened over 100 years ago by Tajima Juroji, with hearth dining and iron-rich baths.

activities.name: Shiohitashi Onsen Ryoma Park
activities.description: Bicarbonate onsen where Sakamoto Ryoma honeymooned, with museum, matchmaking footbath, and his reputed bathtub.

activities.name: Forest Therapy Road
activities.description: Kirishima forest, first in Kagoshima certified as a forest therapy base in March 2007, with four courses.

activities.name: Mount Karakuni
activities.description: Kirishima's highest peak, 1,700 m, with a 900 m diameter, 300 m deep crater and excellent summit views.

activities.name: Hinatayama Saigo-don Village
activities.description: Hinatayama Onsen area loved by Saigo Takamori, with garden, local food, foot bath, and projection mapping.

activities.name: Kirishima City Children's Hall (Former Kokubu High-Tech Observatory)
activities.description: In Uenohara Techno Park east of Kirishima City, a 200-meter plateau views the Kirishima range, Sakurajima, and Kinko Bay.

activities.name: Wakamiko-bana Promenade
activities.description: Coastal one-kilometer path where Yamato Takeru allegedly landed, with Sakurajima views, rocks, and tree roots.

activities.name: Kagoshima Airport 36 Country Club
activities.description: Overlooks the Kirishima mountains. Airport Course stresses strategy; Yokogawa Course fits casual modern golf.

activities.name: Kirishima Golf Club
activities.description: Highly strategic course in Kirishima-Kinkowan National Park, viewing Sakurajima in Kinko Bay and Kirishima peaks.

activities.name: La Vista Kirishima Hills
activities.description: Southern European-style building in Kirishima Onsen overlooking Kinko Bay and Sakurajima. All rooms have open-air onsen baths.

activities.name: Kirishima Sakura Fruit Land
activities.description: Japan's top fruit paradise for grape and pear picking, barbecue, Satsuma dishes, jam making, and farm stays.

activities.name: Satsuma Tinware Craft Museum
activities.description: Make a one-of-a-kind tin plate, continuing the Satsuma Domain's 300-year tin craft tradition.

activities.name: Kirishima City Tourist Information Ashiyu Kirishima
activities.description: Free foot bath, a simple hot spring, at the tourist office in front of Kirishima Jingu's grand torii.

activities.name: Anraku Onsen Myoban-yu
activities.description: Well-cleaned indoor bath floor is reddish-brown from minerals. Handmade open-air bath. Hydrogen carbonate spring.

activities.name: Yugoya Monogatari Family Onsen
activities.description: Private family baths of free-flowing spring water, themed on fairy tales and the Pillow Book.

activities.name: Saigo-don Yu
activities.description: Indoor bath loved by locals; Saigo Takamori used it whenever he visited.

activities.name: Daimyoji Valley Park
activities.description: Waterside valley park of natural potholes and stone paving. Summer play area for children, with falls, paths, and a plaza.

activities.name: Koshikano Beautiful Skin Onsen
activities.description: Kirishima inn with a naturally gushing carbonated spring; all rooms have flowing baths, plus glamping.

activities.name: Old Folk House Tomoko no Uta
activities.description: Renovated 1947 folk house inn and cafe; spring water is fetched daily from a nearby source.

activities.name: Iyashi no Yu Sansui
activities.description: Japanese garden among flowering trees. Twenty-one private baths, each with indoor and open-air baths. Sodium bicarbonate spring.

activities.name: Old Folk House Village Family Bath Tenku
activities.description: Reuses Taisho-era fittings. Detached rooms have old furniture, hearths, dry saunas, and cold baths. Sodium bicarbonate spring.

activities.name: The Pulse Kirishima
activities.description: Activities, suites, family rooms, quality onsen, and lavish meals on grounds exceeding 50,000 square meters.

sights.name: Maizuru Castle Ruins
sights.description: Stone walls, moat, and two stone bridges remain; Shimazu Yoshihisa resided here seven years from 1604.

sights.name: Uenohara Jomon Forest
sights.description: Preserves Uenohara, Japan's oldest and largest-class Jomon settlement site, with pottery, stone tools, and dioramas.

sights.name: Takaya-no-yama-no-e Mausoleum
sights.description: Mausoleum of Hikohohodemi no Mikoto atop a 390-meter peak among cedar trees, near the airport.

sights.name: Iwado Kannon
sights.description: Nanbokucho-period tuff niche near Yokogawa with seated Amida and standing Kannon and Seishi.

sights.name: Ara Shrine
sights.description: One of the five Osumi shrines, founded around 708, where deities and Kannon are enshrined together.

sights.name: Maruo Falls
sights.description: A 23 m high, 16 m wide hot-spring waterfall along Route 223, milky blue and lit up at night.

sights.name: Inukai Falls
sights.description: 36-meter-high, 22-meter-wide white falls against Takachiho Peak, viewed by Sakamoto Ryoma.

sights.name: Wake Shrine
sights.description: Dedicated to Wake no Kiyomaro, with a Sakamoto Ryoma honeymoon monument.

sights.name: Kirishima Mountains
sights.description: Volcanic mountains across Kagoshima and Miyazaki with caldera lakes, seasonal flowers, and many hikers.

sights.name: Kirishima Jingu
sights.description: Vermilion shrine enshrining Ninigi-no-Mikoto; main halls designated a National Treasure in 2022.

sights.name: Mount Takachiho
sights.description: A 1574-meter cone volcano with a heavenly descent legend, a summit spear, superb views, and hiking trails.

sights.name: Kagoshima Jingu
sights.description: Hilltop shrine to Hikohohodemi overlooking Sakurajima; 1756 halls are Important Cultural Properties.

sights.name: Hayatozuka
sights.description: National historic site with three five-story pagodas and four guardian statues, restored near its form from 800 years ago.

sights.name: Kumaso Cave
sights.description: Cave said to be the home of Kumaso chief Kawakami Takeru, 22 m deep. Closed after August 2025 heavy rain.

sights.name: Miyaura Shrine (Fukuyama Married Ginkgo Trees)
sights.description: Historic shrine listed in the Engishiki, with two ginkgo trees over 1,000 years old, a prefectural cultural property.

sights.name: Former Tanaka Family Villa
sights.description: Villa completed in 1922 by Tanaka Shozo, now a prefectural tangible cultural property, with a Japanese garden.

sights.name: Matsushita Museum of Art
sights.description: Founded in 1983 with about 3,000 artworks, from Kuroda Seiki to Monet and Picasso, plus a Japanese garden.

sights.name: Sakamoto Ryoma and Oryo Honeymoon Onsen Monument
sights.description: Marks Ryoma and Oryo's Shiohitashi Onsen stay on Saigo's advice; called Japan's first honeymoon. In Ryoma Park.

sights.name: Hayatozuka Historic Site Museum
sights.description: Guidance hall for national historic site Hayatozuka, showing excavation photos, a Heian Buddha, and a restored stone tower.

sights.name: Inariyama Park
sights.description: Famous for about 100 Yoshino cherry trees, best viewed from late March to early April.

sights.name: Yamagano Gold Mine
sights.description: Prospered with neighboring Nagano as a gold mine supporting Satsuma, leaving many tunnel and facility remains.

sights.name: Wake Park Wisteria
sights.description: One hundred wisteria of 23 varieties, gifted from Okayama's Wake Town, bloom colorfully from mid-April to early May.

sights.name: Osumi-Yokogawa Station
sights.description: Kagoshima's oldest wooden station building, opened in 1903, a national registered tangible cultural property with wartime bullet marks.

sights.name: Miyama-kirishima Bloom
sights.description: Mid to late May at Takachiho-gawara, late May to early June at Ebino, early to late June at Karakunidake.

sights.name: Kokubu Second Base Special Attack Exhibition Room
sights.description: Exhibition of Kokubu Second Base special-attack members' portraits, wills, and relics inside Mizobe Community Center.

sights.name: Kareigawa Station
sights.description: Wooden station opened in 1903, a registered tangible cultural property; popular lunch sold weekends and holidays.

sights.name: Oizumi Spring
sights.description: Abundant spring water averages 15 degrees Celsius and 22 tons per minute, with a gazebo and hand pump.

sights.name: Miyama Concert Area
sights.description: Not only music; enjoy the Kirishima mountains while viewing autumn leaves.

sights.name: Takachiho-gawara
sights.description: Riverbed on Mount Takachiho's west foot with Kirishima Shrine's old site, where the peak and autumn leaves stand out.

sights.name: Tree Tunnel along Prefectural Road 480
sights.description: The contrast of autumn leaves in the forest belt and gentle autumn sunlight through the trees is exquisite.

sights.name: Shinkawa Gorge Area
sights.description: Walking path closed for now after August 2025 heavy rain; Amori River foliage area with hot spring villages.

sights.name: Yokogawa Zelkova
sights.description: Haraiyama zelkova plantation about 4 km from Osumi-Yokogawa Station turns red and yellow; views differ by spot.
